01 / 05Health food & proteinBrand Identity · Packaging · DigitalFull board

Good Shift

Make healthy feel like everyday food.

The challenge

In a category dominated by clinical aesthetics and gym-first messaging, Good Shift needed a visual identity that made protein and health foods feel approachable, energetic and part of everyday life.

The approach

I developed a bold, flexible visual language using expressive typography, a bright colour palette, organic shapes and food-led imagery. The system was designed to carry a consistent personality across packaging, social media and digital touchpoints.

The idea

“Healthy habits, without the hard sell.”

Deliverables

  • Logo & brand elements
  • Protein pouches
  • Tumblers & stickers
  • Social posts
  • Website
  • Tote bag & merch

02 / 05Everyday assistance appBrand Identity · App UI · CampaignFull board

Hei Buddy

Make everyday assistance feel human.

The challenge

Hei Buddy needed to feel like a dependable everyday companion rather than another utility app. Its identity had to translate across digital interfaces, physical brand touchpoints and everyday Indian environments.

The approach

I explored a friendly brand language built around an approachable character, warm colours and recognisable visual elements. The system connects the personality of the brand with its digital experience while maintaining clarity across applications.

The idea

“A little help, built around people.”

Deliverables

  • Logo & character
  • App screens
  • Outdoor & social campaign
  • Stationery
  • Bags & co-branding
  • Storefront

03 / 05Business technologyBrand Identity · Visual System · DigitalFull board

ICCS

Bring a human perspective to business technology.

The challenge

ICCS needed an identity that communicated technological capability without feeling impersonal. The challenge was to balance corporate credibility with a more human and approachable visual presence.

The approach

I developed a visual direction using layered blues, indigo tones and gradient treatments, then extended the identity across digital interfaces, presentation materials, stationery and environmental applications.

The idea

“Growth, engineered with a human perspective.”

Deliverables

  • Logo & sub-brands
  • Colour system
  • Stationery & ID card
  • Website & app icon
  • Outdoor & signage

04 / 05Real estate & infrastructureBrand Identity · Signage · DigitalPreview · full board on request

Vega Group

One identity. Multiple business worlds.

The challenge

Vega Group operates across commercial, government, hospitality and residential projects. Its identity needed to establish a consistent parent brand while accommodating distinct business lines and project identities.

The approach

I developed a visual direction centred on a star-inspired mark, navy and burnt-orange colours, and architectural imagery. The system was designed to maintain recognition across signage, stationery, digital applications and related project brands.

The idea

“We foresee. We create. We care.”

Deliverables

  • Star mark & logo
  • Campaign imagery
  • Billboard & signage
  • Stationery
  • Website
  • Project sub-brands

05 / 05Food staples (atta & dal)Brand Identity · Packaging · RetailFull board

Netpure

Make everyday staples worth trusting.

The challenge

Staples like atta and dal are bought on trust and habit, and look alike on a shelf. Netpure needed an identity that felt dependable and premium while staying familiar to everyday Indian households.

The approach

I developed a bilingual brand system in English and Hindi, built on a confident red and green palette, warm kitchen photography and a dotted map of India. The identity extends from packaging to shopfronts, billboards, stationery and press advertising.

The idea

“The Rhythm of Indian Rasoi.”

Deliverables

  • Bilingual logo (English / Hindi)
  • Atta & dal packaging
  • Billboards & press ads
  • Social posts
  • Retail & shopfront
  • Uniform & stationery

I’m Roshan, a brand designer at Moshi Moshi. My work spans brand identities, packaging and digital experiences for clients across industries.

Having worked across 30+ clients, I’ve learned to approach each project as more than a visual exercise. I’m interested in understanding the problem, finding the right creative direction and building a visual system that holds together wherever the brand shows up.

My background in Interactive Technologies at Atria University, where I studied on a full scholarship, gave me a multidisciplinary foundation across brand identity, UI/UX, product and industrial design. It continues to shape how I approach design — balancing visual expression with usability and the realities of physical and digital applications.

I’m looking to keep growing alongside ambitious designers and creative teams, contributing thoughtful work from the first idea through to its execution.
